story.headline: Ukraine launches 600 drones at Russia
story.summary: Ukraine sent hundreds of drones deep into Russia overnight into 16 August, killing at least six, while Russian missiles struck Kyiv, Kryvyi Rih and Sumy.
story.display_body: Ukraine launched one of its largest aerial attacks of the war overnight into Sunday 16 August, sending hundreds of drones deep into Russia and killing at least six people, while Russian missiles and drones again pounded Ukrainian cities. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said around 600 drones were detected heading for the capital, a third of them shot down over the Moscow region; Russia's Defence Ministry claimed it destroyed 822 Ukrainian drones across the country overnight. In Moscow Oblast an 83-year-old man was killed and a warehouse of the online retailer Wildberries in the village of Koledino was set ablaze, regional governor Andrey Vorobyov said, adding that air defences intercepted 187 drones over the oblast in "one of the most massive" attacks on it in memory. Five more people were killed when over 150 drones hit three towns in the southwestern Rostov region, damaging a railway station and sparking a forest fire. On the Ukrainian side, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said a Russian missile strike on Kryvyi Rih killed two and wounded 14, another person was killed in Sumy, and fires broke out across Kyiv — including at a city book market — injuring six. The exchange extends an escalating pattern of long-range strikes now nearly 4½ years into Russia's full-scale invasion, with Ukraine increasingly targeting Russian military industry, energy sites and Wildberries depots.
story.why: with no ceasefire in sight, both sides are widening deep-strike campaigns that bring the war home to Russian civilians while keeping Ukrainian cities under nightly fire. (AP, 16 Aug 2026; Moscow Oblast detail

story.headline: Colombia asks Trump to pause tariffs
story.summary: Colombia's president asked Trump to suspend US tariffs to aid quake recovery as the 10 August earthquake toll neared 294.
story.display_body: Colombia's new president, Abelardo de la Espriella, said Saturday 15 August he had asked Donald Trump to temporarily suspend US tariffs on Colombian goods to help businesses recover from the deadly 10 August earthquake, as the death toll neared 294. De la Espriella said he spoke with Trump for about ten minutes and that the US president offered condolences over the magnitude-7.4 quake, which struck near San José del Palmar in the Chocó department at 07:34 local time on Monday 10 August (US Geological Survey). Washington raised its tariff on most Colombian products from 10% to 12.5% in late July, exempting a few goods such as coffee and oil; the president said he asked Trump "to consider temporarily suspending the high tariffs… to give some relief to our business owners." Rescuers, meanwhile, pulled a three-year-old girl alive from the rubble roughly 100 hours after the quake.
story.why: it links disaster relief to a live trade dispute, and the still-climbing toll shows how much of the mountainous, hard-to-reach epicentre remains under-served days on. (Al Jazeera, 15 Aug 2026; quake parameters

story.headline: Belgium fights record wildfire
story.summary: A wildfire in Belgium's High Fens park became the largest in the country's modern history, burning over 3,000 hectares and forcing evacuations near the German border.
story.display_body: A wildfire in the High Fens nature park of eastern Belgium has become the largest in the country's modern history, scorching more than 3,000 hectares (7,500 acres) by Sunday 16 August and forcing hundreds from their homes near the German border. The blaze broke out Friday 14 August in an area of fragile peatlands (waterlogged, carbon-rich soils that smoulder and are notoriously hard to extinguish) and pine forest, and exploded from about 80 hectares on Friday to over 3,000 by Sunday morning, local authorities said — an area last devastated by fire in 1911, during a comparable heatwave and drought. Roughly 600 residents of Sourbrodt and Bütgenbach were ordered to evacuate, with a gymnasium in Malmedy opened as a shelter and the Belgian Red Cross on site; the EU dispatched helicopters and water-bombing aircraft after Belgium activated the bloc's civil-protection mechanism. Officials said the rugged terrain was preventing crews from fighting the fire up close by their usual methods.
story.why: it is one more marker of the extreme, Europe-wide heat-and-drought summer already parching Swiss forests and rivers — and peatland fires are especially stubborn and carbon-heavy.

story.headline: Polish tourist bus crash kills 12 in Hungary
story.summary: A Polish tourist bus travelling from Serbia overturned on Hungary's M3 motorway on 16 August, killing at least 12.
story.display_body: At least 12 people were killed and 10 seriously injured when a Polish tourist bus overturned on Hungary's M3 motorway on Sunday 16 August. The coach, travelling from Serbia to Poland with 57 passengers and two drivers, veered off a straight stretch near Mezőkeresztes, about 140 km east of Budapest, and rolled into a ditch; police said the driver, now in custody, likely fell asleep. Eleven people died at the scene and one in hospital, and rescuers pulled some passengers out through the windows.

story.headline: Dittli seeks re-election in Vaud
story.summary: Vaud minister Valérie Dittli announced a 2027 re-election bid despite resistance within her own Centre party.
story.display_body: Vaud finance minister Valérie Dittli announced on Saturday 15 August that she will run again for the cantonal government in 2027, despite open resistance inside her own party. The centrist, whose term has been marked by leaks, forged documents, internal feuds and criminal proceedings, must first secure the backing of Centre Vaud at a party vote on 2 September before she can campaign. "I'm running to win," she told reporters, defending her record through what Le Temps described as a tumultuous, sometimes brutal legislature.
story.why: it sets up a contested re-election fight for one of the canton's most divisive officeholders, and forces her party to decide publicly whether to stand behind her.

story.headline: Union threatens Swiss-EU treaty deal
story.summary: Travail.Suisse said it could help defeat the Switzerland-EU treaty package if parliament weakens the agreed wage-protection measures.
story.display_body: The president of Switzerland's second-largest union federation warned that it could help defeat the Switzerland–EU treaty package if parliament waters down wage-protection guarantees. Travail.Suisse president Adrian Wüthrich, whose federation represents about 130,000 workers, told SRF the group backs the package of treaties governing Swiss–EU relations (the "Bilaterals III") "but not at any price," and said rejecting it outright is "of course" an option should the 14 agreed wage-protection measures be diluted. He singled out the Kautionspflicht — a rule requiring companies to post a bond before taking on work in Switzerland — after parliament's Economic Affairs Committee proposed changes; the Council of States is due to weigh the rival commission proposals in the autumn session.
story.why: wage protection is the pivotal domestic condition for the whole EU deal, and union opposition could be enough to sink it at a referendum — the outcome that would shape free movement and Swiss–EU ties for years.

story.headline: Fatal carriage crash in the Engadin
story.summary: A horse-drawn carriage left the trail in Val Roseg near Pontresina on 15 August, killing one and injuring twelve.
story.display_body: One person was killed and twelve injured, two of them seriously, when a horse-drawn carriage left the trail and hit a tree in the Val Roseg above Pontresina on Saturday 15 August. A 60-strong tourist group, split across two carriage teams, was returning from the scenic Upper Engadine valley when the front team went off the path, Graubünden cantonal police said, calling it the worst carriage accident in the canton in years. Investigators currently believe a technical failure caused the crash; police said all members of the group were resident in Switzerland, and the injured were distributed among hospitals across the canton.
